identificationModule.briefTitle: A Study of BL-M14D1 in Combination With Atezolizumab in Patients With Extensive-stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of BL-M14D1 for Injection in Combination With Atezolizumab in Patients With Extensive-stage Small Cell Lung Cancer

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This Phase II study is a clinical study exploring the efficacy and safety of BL-M14D1 in combination with Atezolizumab in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.

armGroups.label: BL-M14D1+ Atezolizumab
armGroups.description: Participants receive BL-M14D1+ Atezolizumab for the first cycle (3 weeks). Participants with clinical benefit could receive additional treatment for more cycles. The administration will be terminated because of disease progression or intolerable toxicity occurring or other reasons.

interventions.name: BL-M14D1
interventions.description: Administration by intravenous infusion for a cycle of 3 weeks.

interventions.name: Atezolizumab
interventions.description: Administration by intravenous infusion for a cycle of 3 weeks.

primaryOutcomes.description: ORR is defined as the percentage of participants, who has a CR (disappearance of all target lesions) or PR (at least a 30% decrease in the sum of diameters of target lesions). The percentage of participants who experiences a confirmed CR or PR is according to RECIST 1.1.

TEAE is defined as any unfavorable and unintended change in the structure, function, or chemistry of the body temporally emerging, or any worsening (i.e., any clinically significant adverse change in frequency and/or intensity) of a pre-existing condition during the treatment of BL-M14D1 . The type, frequency and severity of TEAE will be evaluated during the treatment of BL-M14D1.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by BICR is defined as the time between the date subjects were randomized and the first observation of disease progression (based on BICR's image-based assessment) or death.

The DCR is defined as the percentage of participants who has a CR, PR, or Stable Disease (SD: neither sufficient shrinkage to qualify for PR nor sufficient increase to qualify for progressive disease \[PD: at least a 20% increase in the sum of diameters of target lesions and an absolute increase of at least 5 mm. The appearance of one or more new lesions is also considered PD\]).
The DOR for a responder is defined as the time from the participant's initial objective response to the first date of either disease progression or death, whichever occurs first.
Overall survival (OS) is defined as the time between the day the subject is randomized and the subject's death.
Maximum serum concentration (Cmax) of BL-M14D1 will be investigated.
Time to maximum serum concentration (Tmax) of BL-M14D1 will be investigated.
Ctrough is defined as the lowest serum concentration of BL-M14D1 prior to the next dose will be administered.
Frequency of anti-BL-M14D1 antibody (ADA) will be investigated.
